content: The following are the professional steps for safely removing personal protective equipment (PPE), including a gown, as recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). The responsibility for interpreting and using this information lies with the reader. 1. Always remove PPE under the guidance and supervision of a trained observer or colleague. Separate containers should also be available for reusable items. 2. To remove head and neck coverings, start from the bottom of the hood at the back of the head. Roll the covering from back to front and from the inside to the outside, taking care to avoid contaminating your face. Dispose of the covering safely. 3. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 4. Remove rubber boots without touching them directly. If overshoes are worn, remove them instead. 5. Carefully remove gloves using an appropriate technique to avoid contamination, and dispose of them safely. 6. Perform hand hygiene again. 7. Remove the gown by first untying the knot, then pulling it from back to front. Roll the gown from the inside to the outside and dispose of it safely. 8. Remove the mask from behind the head. First, untie the bottom string above the head and let it hang in front. Then untie the top string from behind the head. Dispose of the mask safely. 9. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 10. Remove the outer pair of gloves and dispose of them safely, using the technique described earlier. 11. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands again. 12. Remove the apron by leaning forward and taking care to avoid contaminating your hands. For disposable aprons, tear the apron off at the neck and roll it down without touching the front area. Then untie the back and roll the apron forward for safe disposal. 13. Perform hand hygiene after completing the removal of all PPE. By following these detailed steps, the risk of contamination during the removal of PPE is minimized, ensuring the safety of healthcare workers and others in the environment.
